title: Booking agencies after Alexander, and Helen Humes
summary: Fields lists the agencies that booked him, including Joe Artis and the Ferguson Brothers, and a tour with Helen Humes.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: After the Willard Alexander, John Hammond thing kind of played out, who booked your band those years after that?
Numerous others, I'd say, to tell you the truth, ten. Maybe that's why I didn't get any higher. I did most of it and Joe Artis (phonetic spelling) Corporation

did quite a bit of booking for me, and then this negro agency, Ferguson Brothers out of Indiana did quite a bit. I think Clarence Love had introduced--had recommended them--and they did some booking. During that time I did a short tour with Helen Humes, she was a feature.
You weren't aware that she died?
I'll say one thing, she did stage a comeback, because she was wonderful.

Stanley Dance convinced her to come back in 1972 or 1973 to play the Newport Jazz Festival with Count Basie, and her career came full cycle, all the way back. In many ways, she became bigger than she ever was because she was such a great artist.
